title: Tankers Struck

source.title: Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack
source.byline: Al Jazeera Staff, AFP, AP and Reuters (a wire digest)
source.note: published 11-05 18:47 (page time, zone unstated; updated 18:50); the 11-05 sweep matched it on 'diesel' (hormuz, strait of, tanker) and 'iran'. Read in full on 11-06 via the cloud fetch as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. Twenty-one body paragraphs, no subheads, no dateline: the IRGC via Fars, the army via IRNA, UKMTO via the British military, Nakilat, Qatar's foreign ministry, the NYT's unnamed Pentagon officials, Khamenei, Karami. Chosen as the newest row in the queue on an object with a live window (H6, the Strait) — the protocol's first criterion; one Al Jazeera per day; my call

object.label: H6 — US control of the Strait of Hormuz (PG01, proposed 10-15), read from the water the day after the vote: five tankers and a tugboat on fire inside twenty-four hours by Iran's own account — a large tanker on a mine in the 'illegal passageway' south of the strait Wednesday night (IRGC, Fars), a supertanker halted by fire leaving the eastern strait and the tug that came for it (IRGC), three more on naval mines east of the strait Thursday morning and noon (the army, IRNA) — and one hit the instrument can date and place: a tanker struck by two projectiles at 23:20 GMT Wednesday, 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash-Shamal, Qatar (UKMTO), hull and flag unnamed, no claim. Traffic restricted since late February through water that normally carries a fifth of the world's oil; attacks near a record pace and UKMTO 'struggling to accurately report' them because ships no longer report. Qatar mediating; the NYT's unnamed Pentagon officials have US forces poised to resume major combat on the holder's orders; Khamenei and an IRGC commander answer. The pump, the price, the deal and the holder's own words are not on the page

transformNote: the shadow is 'U.S. control' of the Strait (the holder, 10-12 onward) and at its strongest the office's 'oil flows out of the Persian Gulf exceed pre-conflict levels' (aj 11-02, +0.7). H6's falsifier as drafted 10-15 — a commercial vessel sunk or disabled in the Strait — was first sighted on fox 10-20 by Iran's claim (two tankers on mines, 10-17). This page carries the falsifier's terms five times over in one day, again by Iran's claim, and once by an instrument (UKMTO's projectile strike off Qatar — outside the strait proper, in the Gulf). The cut does not rule H6: it reports that the lock's other holder is now naming the passage 'illegal' and 'violating' as it hits hulls, which is control asserted from Tehran's end in the vocabulary of a customs post. Nothing on the page names a hull, an owner, an insurer or a tracker; UKMTO says the count itself is now unreliable

lines.quote: Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack; five oil tankers and a tugboat have caught fire in several incidents, Iranian forces say
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek): the claim attributed ('Iran says'), the hulls counted but unnamed; the vehicle is 'fears of new US attack' — the force in the hed before the water
lines.zWhy: tankers struck in the strait, on the lock-holder's claim, is the water not open

lines.quote: at least five tankers damaged in the Strait of Hormuz, per Iranian forces, who say shipping stays at risk while the war is unresolved
lines.note: the lede: the count and the condition — risk tied to the war's end, by the lock's other holder, in the article's voice
lines.zWhy: shipping at risk while the war is unresolved is the strait held, not controlled

lines.quote: since the war began in late February Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption
lines.note: the record line: the object sized and dated — the most fluid line in the article's own voice
lines.zWhy: traffic severely restricted by Tehran since February is control from the other end

lines.quote: a large oil tanker trying to pass through the 'illegal passageway' south of the strait struck a mine last night, caught fire and was halted
lines.note: constitutive — THE LOCK FROM TEHRAN'S END: the passage named illegal, the mine its enforcement (the IRGC to Fars). Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern strait; a tugboat that approached to fight it also caught fire
lines.note: constitutive — the second and third hulls, no cause given for the fire. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: a 'violating' oil tanker in an unsafe area east of the strait struck a naval mine early Thursday; around noon two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire
lines.note: constitutive — the army's three (via IRNA): 'violating' is the customs-post word; three hulls on mines in a morning. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: a tanker was struck by two projectiles at 23:20 GMT Wednesday, about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar's Madinat ash-Shamal (UKMTO, via the British military)
lines.note: THE INSTRUMENT'S LINE: the one hit on the page with a clock and a bearing — in the Gulf, not the strait; the page's second most fluid line
lines.zWhy: a tanker struck by projectiles off Qatar is the water unsafe beyond the strait

lines.quote: UKMTO did not identify the tanker or its flag state; no immediate claim of responsibility
lines.note: the gap stated as a gap — the most fluid line on the page
lines.zWhy: a strike with no hull named and no claim reads neither way, barely

lines.quote: a Qatari tanker was hit by 'unidentified objects' last week: Nakilat's LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck on October 30, no injuries, no environmental impact, operational
lines.note: later sighting of the Qatari LNG hit (aj 11-01); the one named hull on the page is last week's
lines.zWhy: a named hull hit last week and still operating is the water unsafe but moving

lines.quote: attacks on Gulf tankers still running close to a record pace; UKMTO said last month it was 'struggling to accurately report' the true number because most ships now refuse to report
lines.note: the instrument names its own blind spot — the count on this page is a floor, by the counter's own admission
lines.zWhy: an instrument that cannot count the attacks is the water's state unknown and worsening

lines.quote: Qatar has stepped up mediation to resume talks on ending the war; the foreign ministry's spokesperson said Tuesday both sides were reviewing mediator proposals and talks were continuing
lines.note: the reopening's door, as the page carries it — a date (Tuesday), no terms
lines.zWhy: talks continuing through Qatar is the water's reopening in negotiation, slightly toward open

lines.quote: unnamed Pentagon officials and commanders told the New York Times Wednesday that thousands of US air and naval forces are poised to resume major combat against Iran on the president's orders
lines.note: the force, relayed from another paper's unnamed sources — the hed's 'fears' sourced; the article's highest line after the hed
lines.zWhy: forces poised to resume combat is the strait's state unsettled, toward not open

lines.quote: Iranian government and military leaders warned of repercussions if the US or Israel pursue further military action
lines.note: the frame for the two closing constitutive lines
lines.zWhy: repercussions warned is the other holder's lock restated

lines.quote: there should not be 'even the slightest inclination towards submission' to the US, which will stay hostile no matter which party governs
lines.note: constitutive — a later sighting of C-khamenei-1104-no-lever (the vote changes nothing). Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: continued 'hostile and brutal actions' by Iran's enemies would bring 'further Iranian victories', accelerating the expulsion of foreign powers and the collapse of Israel
lines.note: constitutive — the IRGC Ground Force commander; the page's last word. Not Dia-scored
